controls: A permanently installed CEMS is used for compliance monitoring
Apply EN 14181 quality assurance to the installed CEMS.
Treating a permanent compliance CEMS as an informal process sensor
A DAHS is associated with CEMS
Do not claim EN 14181 alone assures the DAHS; apply the separate DAHS control standard.
Assuming analyser QA automatically validates data handling
A CEMS is selected for a permit measurand
Require MCERTS certification at an appropriate certification range for QAL1 evidence.
Using certification at an irrelevant range
Use QAL2 procedures to verify correct installation and calibrate against standard reference methods.
Accepting factory setup without site calibration
A newly installed CEMS enters service
Complete functional tests including linearity, zero drift and span drift checks.
Starting compliance reporting before functional testing
A CEMS operates between QAL2 and AST exercises
Regularly measure and record drift and precision under QAL3.
An AST shows the calibration function is no longer valid
Investigate, correct as needed and perform another QAL2.
Continuing to use an invalid calibration function
Multiple suppliers and laboratories support the CEMS
Keep overall EN 14181 compliance responsibility with the operator.
Transferring legal responsibility to a contractor
A laboratory performs QAL2 or AST reference measurements
Require the relevant ISO/IEC 17025, SRM and EN 14181 accreditation scope.
Using an accredited laboratory outside its scope
A QAL2 or AST campaign is scheduled
Ensure mandatory functional tests occur before parallel SRM tests.
Calibrating against SRMs before confirming instrument function
The CEMS is in routine operation
Maintain and apply an operator-owned QAL3 procedure.
Leaving QAL3 entirely to the annual test laboratory
QAL2, QAL3 and AST records are produced
Retain reports and supporting records for the period specified by the regulator.
A test laboratory conducts EN 14181 work
Participate in available proficiency-testing schemes and maintain required proficiency.
A laboratory spreadsheet calculates QAL2 or AST results
Control the spreadsheet within the laboratory quality system.
The permit requires continuous monitoring of a determinand
Select a CEMS certified for that exact measurand.
A certified CEMS is evaluated for the site
Confirm the certified range is suitable for the expected application.
Choosing a range that weakens required performance
Confirm site and stack conditions do not reduce performance below the required standard.
Require evidence it is proven on comparable installations.
Using an unproven application without evidence
A CEMS is procured or installed
Require provisions for post-installation zero, span and linearity tests.
Installing equipment that cannot be functionally tested
Require means to check leaks and response time near the sampling probe.
Testing only the analyser while bypassing the sampling train
Store certification range separately from the full measurement range.
Treating any measurable value as certified performance
A selected range may cap process peaks
Reject peak capping unless an exceptional case is agreed with the regulator in advance.
The routine CEMS range is configured
Set it from the applicable ELV and expected peaks, not merely the narrow range observed during QAL2.
Configuring an artificially narrow operating range
More than one range setting is needed to capture operating conditions
Verify supplementary higher ranges used for monitoring.
Existing CEMS ranges are unsuitable and QAL2/AST/QAL3 fail
Replace with suitably ranged CEMS within the stated one-year route.
An alternative extractive sampling component is proposed
Require independent performance evidence and the same general sampling technique.
Replacing a permeation dryer with a materially different chiller system
SRM spread and scatter cannot support a calibration function
Use documented alternative calibration means rather than inventing a regression.
A CEMS failure triggers investigation and repair
Complete investigation, repair and retesting within six months.
A CEMS or SRM sampling location is chosen
Apply EN 15259 representativeness, access and non-interference requirements.
Assess stack homogeneity before QAL2 unless an accepted exception applies.
Assuming a single point represents a heterogeneous stack
Document selection, maintenance, competence, calibration, records, security and continuity procedures.
Managing the CEMS through undocumented practices
CEMS and data-recording devices are accessible
Allowing silent changes to readings or configuration
